title: PlacementX
description: One placement drive connects a recruiter’s brief, a student’s verified profile and the placement office’s selection record.
team: NMIMS capstone project. This repository is a fork of YashChaudhari999/PlacementX.
problem: At NMIMS, staff coordinated recruitment across spreadsheets, email and WhatsApp. A student’s marks, a recruiter’s criteria and the latest application status lived in different places.
solution: The placement office publishes a drive against verified student records. Coordinators review records within their department, while students can follow their applications through selection.
journey: A recruiter submits a drive brief through a token-based form.
The placement office reviews the brief and publishes the eligibility criteria.
A verified student checks eligibility and applies.
Staff record selection rounds and offers. The student can follow the application’s status.
architecture: React and Expo clients share an Express API. Prisma reads and writes placement records in PostgreSQL. Socket.IO delivers live updates, while BullMQ and Redis handle queued notifications.
decision: Recruiters can submit a brief through a scoped link. This keeps occasional external users outside the college account-provisioning workflow while giving staff a review step.
results: The maintainers report a web and API pilot for a single college. The mobile bundle passed their build check. APK and physical-device testing remain pending.
limitations: An earlier Python service handled placement predictions and résumé parsing. The current implementation removed that service and its database fields.

title: AutoMarket
description: A used-car marketplace that connects vehicle discovery, seller intake and appointment booking.
problem: A buyer can narrow a catalogue to one car and still lose the appointment if another request reserves the same slot. Sellers also need a review step before their vehicles enter the catalogue.
solution: Buyers search and compare inventory before booking. Operations staff review seller submissions and manage the service centres where appointments take place.
journey: Search the catalogue by model or city and narrow the results.
Compare vehicles and open a listing to review its details.
Choose an appointment. The API checks ownership and the database enforces booking conflicts.
architecture: The Next.js frontend sends requests to ASP.NET Core. The API owns access to a private PostgreSQL schema and calls an internal FastAPI service for optional intelligence.
decision: Two buyers can request the same slot concurrently. A database constraint enforces exclusivity inside the transaction, so correctness survives simultaneous requests.
results: The implementation-status report records unit tests, database checks and a live end-to-end exercise. Deterministic pricing and recommendation scoring are implemented.
limitations: Photo storage, push delivery and transactional email still require provider configuration. Learned valuation, semantic search and image-condition models await approved data or artifacts.

title: Carbon Footprint AI
description: A lifestyle calculator that estimates annual emissions and explains which changes could reduce them.
problem: A household footprint total gives a reader little guidance about what to change. Energy use, travel and consumption need to be compared on a common annual scale.
solution: The calculator pairs a model estimate with a separate category breakdown. Readers can compare the result with configured benchmarks and inspect possible reductions.
features: Annual estimate in tonnes of CO₂ equivalent
journey: Enter household energy, travel and consumption habits.
Calculate an annual estimate and inspect the category chart.
Review the suggested changes in order of estimated savings.
architecture: Flask serves both the static interface and the prediction API. A validated request feeds an XGBoost pipeline for the total and deterministic calculations for categories and recommended actions.
decision: A single stateless service handles the calculation without storing lifestyle responses. Optional recent summaries stay in the browser. Category calculations remain separate so readers can trace how the explanation was produced.
results: The repository documents separate training, validation and test partitions drawn from formula-generated synthetic data. This evaluates how well the pipeline reproduces the generator.
limitations: Real-world emissions accuracy has not been established. The estimate and suggested savings are educational approximations.

title: CapstoneX
description: A shared review workflow for capstone students, mentors and administrators, from team formation to evaluation.
problem: A proposed topic, its approval history and a mentor’s weekly feedback belong to the same project. Each participant needs access to the part they can act on.
solution: Role-specific screens connect group formation, topic review, mentor allocation and progress reporting. Administrators can review recommendations alongside the supporting evidence.
journey: Students form a group and submit a project topic.
The proposed topic enters review and the group receives a mentor.
The group submits progress updates for mentor review and evaluation.
architecture: Next.js presents the role-specific interfaces. Express handles governance rules and PostgreSQL persistence. Separate FastAPI runtimes serve decision-support requests.
decision: The governed AI workflow records evidence and confidence and retains human approval. A reviewer can inspect a recommendation before it changes a project decision.
results: The readiness matrix records passing backend assertions and frontend type and lint checks. The README documents deployment evidence for the backend and focused AI Team runtime.
limitations: Full-lifecycle authenticated browser coverage, migration and restore verification, and independently reviewed model quality remain open. Deployment of the complete ML workload is unverified.

title: Portfolio Universe
description: A responsive portfolio that brings projects, technical skills and credentials into one reading experience.
problem: A reviewer needs a quick route from a project summary to the work itself, with the same information accessible on a phone.
solution: Featured projects lead into a compact archive. Section navigation also takes visitors directly to skills, experience and credentials.
journey: Browse the featured projects.
Open a project’s source or demo.
Return to download the résumé or use the contact section.

title: File Sharing Website
team: Yash Chaudhari, Kunal Khaire and Chetan Patil
description: Share an uploaded file through a download token or QR code, with optional account history.
problem: A sender needs to hand a file to someone who may have no account or may be using another device.
solution: The Express upload handler stores the file in Supabase Storage and creates a token and QR code for retrieval. An account associates uploads with a sender’s history.
journey: Select and upload a file.
Share its download link or QR code.
The recipient opens the link to retrieve the file.

title: Smart Guard: Attendance System
description: Role-specific attendance views for security guards and the supervisors reviewing their shifts.
problem: Supervisors need an overview across shifts, while an individual guard needs to see their own attendance history.
solution: A Flask application handles attendance records and serves guard-level summaries. The repository also includes Power BI reports for comparative analysis.
journey: Select the guard or supervisor role at sign-in.
Review the guard’s attendance summary or open the supervisor report.
Inspect trends across the recorded shifts.

title: EvolveX System
description: A habit tracker that turns workouts and productivity goals into quests with character progression.
problem: A list of completed habits shows what happened today but gives little sense of progress over time.
solution: Players choose physical or productivity quests, complete tasks and follow changes to their character’s stats and streaks.
journey: Create a player profile.
Complete a daily training or productivity quest.
Review progress and choose the next task.
team: The project credits Antigravity as system designer.

title: SmartCSV: Intelligent CSV Analytics Platform
description: Turn a CSV upload into a cleaned dataset, statistical summaries and a shareable report.
problem: A raw CSV can contain duplicates, missing values and outliers before an analyst has even begun to look for relationships.
solution: A Flask pipeline cleans the table and derives descriptive statistics and correlations. The frontend plots the results and the reporting flow supports shareable links.
journey: Upload a CSV for processing.
Inspect distributions and correlations in the generated report.
Share the findings or ask a dataset question when the Claude integration is configured.

title: House Rent Predictor
description: Estimate monthly rent across five Indian cities using property details and regression models that run in the browser.
problem: Someone comparing rentals needs to see how a change in city, floor area or bedroom count affects an estimated monthly budget.
solution: Python-trained regression coefficients ship with the interface. The browser calculates the estimate from the selected property details without a prediction server.
journey: Choose a city and enter the property details.
Request a monthly rent estimate.
Change the inputs to explore a different property.
limitations: Estimates reflect the training data and the five supported cities. They do not establish the asking price of an individual listing.
